recentItems.title: Why Germany's far-right AfD has surged in popularity | The Current
recentItems.description:
This Sunday, Germans head to the polls in Saxony-Anhalt, where the far-right Alternative for Germany party — or AfD — is surging in the eastern state. If it wins, it would mark the first time a far-right party has held state power in Germany since the Nazis. CBC’s Jessica Singer has been on the ground, following the campaign and speaking with voters in the state capital, Magdeburg.

recentItems.title: The Netherlands takes its gold out of the U.S. | About That
recentItems.description:
The Dutch central bank has quietly moved roughly $10 billion U.S. worth of gold out of the United States Federal Reserve — and $1 billion out of Canada — transferring it to London. Andrew Chang explains why experts say this move could indicate fracturing trust in the U.S. as a safe place to stockpile national assets.
